Tests variable labels against the PV

Source: R/labels.R
label_test.Rd

Compares the variable labels in a field-data dataframe with the labels that follow from the va- and vb-tags of the PV (see pv_var_labels()). One call checks all variables of a module.

Usage

label_test(
  data,
  pv,
  ignore = c("duration$", "_e$"),
  show_format = FALSE,
  show_unmatched = TRUE,
  stop_on_fail = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A neps field-data dataframe, read with haven::read_dta() so that the variables carry their labels.

pv

The result of read_pv(), or a path (or several paths) to PV docx files.

ignore

Character vector of regular expressions. Variables in the data whose names match are not checked. Default: duration variables and variables ending in _e.

show_format

Logical, if TRUE the variables whose labels differ only in formatting are printed as well.

show_unmatched

Logical, if TRUE (default) the variables that are only in the data or only in the PV are listed.

stop_on_fail

Logical, if TRUE (default) the function stops with an error if a label differs. If FALSE it only prints the results, which is handy to get the result table back.

Value

Invisibly a data frame with one row per checked variable and the columns var, pv_var, data_label, pv_label, status ("ok", "format", "truncated", "item_ref", "mismatch", "missing_label", "unclear"), item and note. If labels differ and stop_on_fail = TRUE, the function stops with an error after printing them.

Details

Every variable in data is matched to a variable of the PV by name. Loop variables with a suffix like _1, _2 are matched to the PV variable without the suffix. The label in the data (attribute label, as set by haven::read_dta()) is then compared with the expected label:

  • identical (apart from blanks): fine.

  • different only in brackets, slashes, hyphens, quotes, colons, commas or upper/lower case: fine, counted as a formatting difference. Use show_format = TRUE to list them.

  • the data label is cut off at Stata's limit of 80 characters but otherwise identical: fine.

  • the data label refers to other items by their item number where the PV uses the variable name, e.g. a preload with "(23110)" in the data and "(bvnr)" in the PV: fine, if the item number belongs to exactly that variable in the PV. Counted as an item reference and listed with show_format = TRUE.

  • anything else, or no label at all in the data: ERROR. The function prints the variable with both labels and stops at the end.

Variables for which no label could be derived from the PV are listed as a NOTE with the reason, they do not make the test fail. Variables that are only in the data or only in the PV are listed as a NOTE as well. Variables whose names match one of the regular expressions in ignore are skipped.

See also

Other test functions: ac_test(), date_test_complex(), ef_test(), value_label_test()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
T_26ET <- haven::read_dta("26ET.dta")
pv_26ET <- read_pv("NEPS_B180_SC6_EP_26ET_V2_2_20250312.docx")
label_test(T_26ET, pv_26ET)

# also list the labels that only differ in brackets, hyphens or case
label_test(T_26ET, pv_26ET, show_format = TRUE)

# get the full comparison table without stopping
res <- label_test(T_26ET, pv_26ET, stop_on_fail = FALSE)
res[res$status == "mismatch", ]
} # }
